thread:
maria: Heads up — after the retention flag change on the console canary, invoice-preview sampling disappeared for a subset of tenants. Not a full outage but previews show 0 tokens for some routes.
aj: saw that earlier, thanks. Is this the change that reduced telemetry retention from 7d -> 1d for sampled events?
kai: yep, that toggle got flipped in the canary to save storage costs. It was scoped to namespace `console-sample-*`.
maria: the problem seems to be we rely on sampled telemetry to backfill invoice previews in the UI; if samples are gone we show zeros instead of the best-effort estimate. UX is confusing customers.
ryan: rough. Do we have a fallback from the aggregate ledger for previews? I thought previews were computed from the sample store + heuristics.
aj: previews prefer samples for accuracy; fallback uses hourly aggregates but those are delayed by the ingest window and don't include per-route tags in some cases. Hence the zeros.
maria: proposal: revert retention change in canary, then deploy a guard in the preview API that returns a stale-but-plausible estimate if samples are missing. Thoughts?
kai: revert is fine short-term. Long-term we need a policy: either keep samples for 7d for tiers with previews OR move preview logic to rely on faster aggregates.
ryan: moving logic is trickier — it requires route-tag propagation to the hourly aggregator which is not guaranteed for some legacy proxies.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback started by @maria — 1 step remaining.
maria: thanks @sre-bot. Also I want to raise an internal API debate: should we expose retention as a per-tenant config in the console? Ops wants it internal-only to limit support overhead. Billing/product wants per-tenant because enterprise customers asked for longer sample retention to audit invoices.
aj: exposing it to customers introduces support vectors (e.g., people toggling to 30d and causing big storage). We could expose a tiered UI: editable for enterprise, locked for self-serve.
kai: agree with AJ. Implementation detail: retention is enforced at ingestion tagger (edge-proxy), which sets a sample TTL header. We can add allowed-max per-tenant in the tenant config service.
ryan: that approach keeps control. We also need console UX: show a clear badge when preview is using aggregated fallback vs sample-based. That prevents confusion.
maria: good call. Add ephemeral banner: "Preview uses aggregated estimates — for accurate preview enable extended telemetry or wait for hourly aggregates."
aj: telemetry volume note — if we allow 7d for many tenants it increases storage by ~3x based on current sampling rates. We should pair retention toggles with smarter retention policies, like: retain full samples for 24h, keep route headers for 7d but compact payloads.
kai: can do: compacted samples schema v2 — strip heavy context, keep token counts + route/tags + payload hash. Storage savings ~60%. Need migration plan for read path.
maria: action items: 1) rollback canary retention change (in progress). 2) add preview fallback banner and heuristic answer. 3) design tenant retention policy in tenant-config service (max allowed per tier). 4) evaluate compacted-sample schema for long-term.
ryan: I'll open a tiny RFC with UX mock for the banner + API shape for the fallback field: { "preview_mode": "samples|aggregates", "estimated_tokens": 1234, "estimated_confidence": 0.65 }
aj: also add metrics: `preview.source` tag (samples/aggregates/fallback) so dashboard can chart how often previews are degraded.
kai: will sketch the ingestion header change and a migration runbook. Suggest we run a two-week pilot for compacted samples on lower-cost tenants.
maria: cool. If rollback finishes cleanly and previews return to normal we still need to schedule the RFC + follow-ups. Putting this on the eng-platform weekly cadence.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback completed for `canary/console-sample-toggle` by @maria. 7123456820.
billing-bot: alert: a single enterprise tenant requested extended retention for audit last week; ticket #BILL-1123.
maria: OK noted. I'll add BILL-1123 to the RFC stakeholders. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
